# create-image

Use this skill when generating multiple images so the set stays cohesive and production-quality.

## Workflow
1. Decide art direction up front: medium (photo/illustration/3D), color palette, mood. Reuse it for every prompt.
2. Call the `create_image` tool with detailed prompts: subject, composition, lighting, style, palette.
3. Read the returned file path to inspect each generated image.
4. Regenerate with explicit fixes when an image misses the mark ("make the lighting warmer", "add a runner in the foreground").
5. Reference the saved files (e.g. `./images/...`) from the page markup.

## Prompt quality
- Be specific about subject, setting, camera/art style, lighting, and palette.
- For web use prefer wide sizes (1024x1792 portrait / 1792x1024 landscape) over square.

# opencode-create-image

Generate images from any OpenAI-compatible API directly inside opencode. The plugin registers a single `create_image` tool so the agent can generate and save images on its own — no manual commands, no copying URLs.

## What it does

The agent calls `create_image` whenever a page or piece of visual content needs imagery. The agent writes the prompt itself, the plugin generates the image through your configured API endpoint, saves it to disk, and returns the absolute file path (plus a file attachment). The agent can then drop that file into the page it is building.

### Example: fitness app landing page

You ask opencode to build a landing page for a fitness app. During the build the agent needs a hero image, so it calls `create_image` itself:

- The agent writes a detailed prompt ("runner crossing a finish line at sunrise, energetic motion, bold backlighting, saturated coral and indigo palette, magazine-style sports photography") and calls `create_image` with `size: "1792x1024"`.
- The plugin generates the image and returns an absolute path like `C:\path\to\project\images\2026-08-15T10-30-00-000Z-runner-crossing-a-finish-line-at-sunrise.jpg`.
- The agent reads that path, references `./images/...` in the page markup, and moves on to the next image.

This is autonomous plumbing: the plugin handles the API call, the file write, and the path hand-off so the agent can keep building.

## Install

```sh
# global (all projects)
opencode plugin opencode-create-image -g

# current project only
opencode plugin opencode-create-image
```

Or add it to your opencode config in tuple form with options:

```json
{
  "plugin": [["opencode-create-image", { "baseUrl": "...", "model": "..." }]]
}
```

## Configuration

The plugin is configured through plugin options (which win) or environment variables:

| Setting      | Plugin option | Env var              | Default                        |
| ------------ | ------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| API key      | `apiKey`      | `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_KEY` | — (required)       |
| API base URL | `baseUrl`     | `OPENAI_BASE_URL`    | `https://api.openai.com/v1`    |
| Model        | `model`       | `OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL` | `gpt-image-1`                  |
| Size         | `size`        | —                    | `1024x1024`                    |
| Quality      | `quality`     | —                    | `auto`                         |
| Output dir   | `outputDir`   | —                    | `images`                       |

Plugin options always take precedence over environment variables.

### Tool arguments

The `create_image` tool accepts:

- `prompt` (string, required) — detailed description of the image to create
- `size` (enum: `1024x1024`, `1024x1792`, `1792x1024`, `auto`) — optional
- `quality` (enum: `auto`, `standard`, `high`) — optional
- `outputDir` (string) — directory relative to the project dir; defaults to `images`

### Output

Images are saved under `<project>/images/` with timestamped filenames (e.g. `2026-08-15T10-30-00-000Z-hero-runner.jpg`). The tool result returns the absolute file path plus a file attachment so the agent can inspect and reference the image.

## Compatibility

- Works with any OpenAI-compatible API that implements the `/v1/images/generations` endpoint (any provider exposing the standard `/v1/images/generations` shape; Azure OpenAI needs a compatible gateway/proxy, and many local/self-hosted providers).
- Handles both `b64_json` and `url` response formats.

## Companion skill

The repo ships a companion skill in `skills/create-image` that keeps generated image sets cohesive (consistent art direction, prompt quality guidance). Install it by copying the folder into your skills directory:

```sh
cp -r skills/create-image ~/.config/opencode/skills/
```

or add it to your opencode config with a `skills.urls` entry pointing at this repository.

## Development

```sh
bun install
bun run typecheck
bun run test
bun run build
```

# Design: opencode-create-image plugin

## Goal

An opencode plugin (`opencode-create-image`, npm package) that registers a
`create_image` tool. The tool calls any OpenAI-compatible
`/images/generations` endpoint, saves the generated image to disk, and
returns the file path plus a file attachment so the agent can reference the
image (e.g., drop it into a landing page it is building).

## Decisions (user-approved)

- **Distribution:** source on GitHub, package on npm. Install anywhere via
  `opencode plugin opencode-create-image` (add `-g` for global). Optional
  config tuple: `"plugin": [["opencode-create-image", { "baseUrl": "...", "model": "..." }]]`.
- **API:** OpenAI Images API shape, configurable base URL so any
  OpenAI-compatible provider (including local proxies) works.
- **Output:** save image to a file, return the absolute path + a
  `ToolResult` attachment. Fall back to downloading a returned `url` when a
  provider does not return `b64_json`.
- **Configuration:** env vars with plugin-options override
  (`options` from the config tuple). Tool args override per call.
- **Guidance:** plugin-only core; optional companion skill folder shipped in
  the repo (documented, not auto-installed). No system-prompt injection.

## Architecture

Three source files, each one responsibility:

- `src/index.ts` — plugin entry. Exports the `Plugin` function, registers
  the `create_image` tool via `tool()`. Wires config + image generation
  together and builds the `ToolResult`.
- `src/config.ts` — settings resolution: plugin options → env vars →
  defaults.
- `src/image.ts` — HTTP call to `/images/generations` + file save.

### Data flow

1. Agent calls `create_image({ prompt, size?, quality?, outputDir? })`.
2. `index.ts` resolves config once at plugin init.
3. `image.ts` POSTs to `{baseUrl}/images/generations` with
   `response_format: "b64_json"`, `n: 1`, resolved model/size/quality.
4. Response `data[0].b64_json` → Buffer → write to file under
   `<cwd>/<outputDir>/<timestamp>-<slug>.<ext>`. If only `url` present,
   download it instead.
5. Returns `{ output: "Image saved to <abs path>", attachments: [{ type: "file", mime, url, filename }] }`.

### Config resolution (highest → lowest)

| Setting   | Plugin option | Env var                  | Default                  |
| --------- | ------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------ |
| API key   | `apiKey`      | `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_KEY` | none (error if missing) |
| Base URL  | `baseUrl`     | `OPENAI_BASE_URL`        | `https://api.openai.com/v1` |
| Model     | `model`       | `OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL`     | `gpt-image-1`            |
| Size      | `size`        | —                        | `1024x1024`              |
| Quality   | `quality`     | —                        | `auto`                   |
| Output dir| `outputDir`   | —                        | `images`                 |

Tool args `size`, `quality`, `outputDir` override config for that call.

### Error handling

- Missing API key → clear error naming the env vars and the option.
- Non-2xx → error includes status code and response body.
- No `b64_json` and no `url` → descriptive error.
- `context.abort` signal passed to fetch for cancellation.
- Filename includes a timestamp → no collision.

## Packaging

- `type: "module"`, `main`/`exports` → `./dist/index.js`, `types` →
  `./dist/index.d.ts`.
- Built with tsup (ESM bundle), `@opencode-ai/plugin` ^1.18.18 as a runtime
  dependency.
- No `openai` npm SDK — global `fetch` only (Bun/Node built-in), which also
  maximizes compatibility with OpenAI-compatible servers.
- Uses `node:fs/promises` and `node:path` (portable across Bun and Node).

## Testing

- `test/config.test.ts` — defaults, env override, options-over-env.
- `test/image.test.ts` — b64_json decode + write; url fallback download;
  missing-key error; non-2xx error; custom output dir; filename slugging.
  Global `fetch` stubbed with `vi.stubGlobal`.
- `test/index.test.ts` — tool registered; execute writes a file and returns
  an attachment.
- Commands: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run build`.

## Distribution and install

- Repo: GitHub. Install: `opencode plugin opencode-create-image`.
- Manual npm publish (no CI automation for now): bump version, run
  `npm run prepublishOnly`, `npm publish --access public`, tag the repo.
  Documented step-by-step in the README.
- Companion skill: copy `skills/create-image` into
  `~/.config/opencode/skills/` or add a `skills.urls` entry.

## Non-goals

- No `release.yml` CI publish (user wants to publish manually for now).
- No AGENTS.md (user dropped it).
- No system-prompt injection.
- No `n` tool arg (OpenAI-compatible image APIs typically require `n: 1`).
